name: Liuqian Zhuang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Castro, Andy & Bruce Hansen. 2010. Hongshui He Zhuang dialect intelligibility survey. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2010-025. Dallas: SIL International. 110 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5.2 'Tone analysis' (p.19, Table 3) gives the six-tone systems of 'Tonal Region C' = Xiangzhou Dale/Yunjiang, Luzhai Sipai/Luzhai, Wuxuan Huangmao (the Liuqian area); Appendix E p.33 states '(C)V(C)' syllable structure and that Zhuang is 'predominantly monosyllabic'; Appendix K lists tone realizations per data point. a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence = 0 hits.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-027 (split of Northern Zhuang [ccx]) and Request for New Language Code Element 'zlq Zhuang, Liuqian' (S. Tan, 2007-05-28).
sources.note: Nothing (administrative). Defines the language's territory: 'areas east of the Liujiang and north of the Qianjiang rivers, including northern Wuxuan, Xiangzhou, Luzhai and possibly Pingle, Yangshuo and Hezhou'; pop. 370,000.

sources.note: Chinese-language overview of the Zhuang dialects with phonological sketches of representative points; Glottolog (ref 666722, listed by Glottolog as an overview;phonology) lists its points as Qinzhou, Fangcheng, Zhongzuo, Tiandeng, Debao, Yongning, Bama, Dahua and Zhaoping, assigning Zhaoping 昭平 to Liuqian [zlq]. A point phonology in this genre gives initials, finals and tone categories with values, so a Zhaoping tone table is expected, but the book was not opened and Zhaoping lies in the 'possibly' (Hezhou) extension of the zlq area, not in Xiangzhou/Luzhai/N Wuxuan.
